text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - British stocks staged a blistering rally with the lead index chalking up its third record close in as many days to come within grasping distance of the psychologically important 5,000 level. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,964.2, up 64.9 points, or 1.32 percent.

FRANKFURT - German shares held most of their gains over the course of Wednesday afternoon, ending off earlier highs but supported by the unstoppable dollar and bullish news from Wall Street, where the Dow breached 8,000 points for the first time. The DAX-30 index closed at 4,201.24, up 80.11 points, or 1.94 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 4,223.69, up 84.01 points, or 2.03 percent.

PARIS - French shares ended at a closing high on Wednesday, with strong gains in LVMH and SGS-Thomson, but were below an all-time high set earlier in the day. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,988.01, up 37.31 points, or 1.26 percent.

ZURICH - Swiss shares extended early gains near the end of the session to close more than one percent higher as the strong dollar and a favourable domestic interest rate outlook boosted the market, dealers said. The Swiss market index closed at 5927.5, up 82.8 points, or 1.42 percent.

MILAN - Italian shares continued their relentless climb, ending just off new Mibtel and Mib30 Bourse index highs set earlier in the day. Traded volumes were not at a record but seen solid at over 2.5 trillion lire, and foreign investors were seen in the front line. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 14,381, up 277 points, or 1.96 percent.
AMSTERDAM - Dutch shares jumped to a new record close on Wednesday with stocks pushed higher by a firm dollar and a rising Wall Street.
The AEX share index touched a new all-time high at 967.02 points and ended at a new record close of 965.25, 16.09 points or 1.7 percent, higher than Tuesday's close.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks bounced back as bullish technology stocks in New York overnight and the yen's softening against the dollar encouraged investors to seek high-tech issues, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20358.74, up 289.33 points, or 1.44 percent.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed lower on concerns about property prices under the government's increased land supply programme, brokers said. The Hang Seng index closed at 15,446.02, down 41.22 points, or 0.27 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended firmer after active trade, with industrials rising to a record closing high on institutional buying and gold shares down on bullion failing to stay above the $320 per ounce level. The All-share index closed at 7,422.8, up 32.1 points, or 0.43 percent. The All Gold index closed at 969.2, down 7.1 points, or 0.57 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 8936.4, up 50.7 points, or 0.73 percent.
